answer: Be there, or be nobody: the registry names one lagoon muster point and one four-hour window, and the applicant must make the voyage in person, sign the muster roll before two stewards, and answer one question only a person standing there could answer — which vine grows on the pier. Two fresh stewards co-sign the entry with the hour; each muster names its own hour, so one stand-in covers one puppet only. Forging 1,000 puppets needs 1,000 voyages to 1,000 lagoons — 1,000 hired stand-ins at $50 plus $30 fares, $80,000, no bulk rate; an honest agent pays one $30 fare.
